title: Past Simple: Regular and Irregular Verbs
indexDescription: Talk about finished actions and past experiences with regular and irregular verbs.
pageDescription: Talk about the past with regular and irregular verbs
goal: Use the past simple to talk about finished actions and experiences.

content.title: 1) Regular Verbs
content.text: work → worked, play → played, study → studied, watch → watched
content.speakText: worked, played, studied, watched

content.title: 2) Irregular Verbs
content.text: go → went, see → saw, have → had, eat → ate, buy → bought
content.speakText: went, saw, had, ate, bought

content.title: 3) Time Words
content.text: yesterday, last week, last year, two days ago, in 2020
content.speakText: yesterday, last week, last year, two days ago, in 2020

title: Past Simple Questions and Negatives
indexDescription: Ask about the past and make negative past sentences with did/didn't.
pageDescription: Ask and answer questions about the past
goal: Form past simple questions and negatives with did and didn't.

content.title: 1) Questions with Did
content.text: Did you work yesterday? Did she go to school? Did they like it?
content.speakText: Did you work yesterday? Did she go to school? Did they like it?

content.title: 2) Short Answers
content.text: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. Yes, he did. / No, she didn't.
content.speakText: Yes, I did. No, I didn't. Yes, he did. No, she didn't.

content.title: 3) Negatives
content.text: I didn't work. She didn't go. They didn't buy it.
content.speakText: I didn't work. She didn't go. They didn't buy it.

practice.text: Answer only with Yes, I did / No, I didn't.

title: Present Continuous for Now and Arrangements
indexDescription: Talk about actions happening now and future arrangements.
pageDescription: Describe actions now and fixed future plans
goal: Use the present continuous for now and future arrangements.

content.text: I am studying. She is working. They are watching TV.
content.speakText: I am studying. She is working. They are watching TV.

content.title: 2) Future Arrangements
content.text: I am meeting a friend tomorrow. We are flying next week.
content.speakText: I am meeting a friend tomorrow. We are flying next week.

content.title: 3) Form
content.text: am / is / are + verb-ing
content.speakText: am, is, are plus verb I N G

title: Will for Predictions and Offers
indexDescription: Make predictions, offers, and decisions with will.
pageDescription: Use will for future predictions and offers
goal: Use will for predictions, offers, and quick decisions.

content.title: 1) Predictions
content.text: It will rain tomorrow. You will love this film.
content.speakText: It will rain tomorrow. You will love this film.

content.title: 2) Offers and Decisions
content.text: I will help you. I'll open the window. We'll call you later.
content.speakText: I will help you. I'll open the window. We'll call you later.

content.title: 3) Negatives and Questions
content.text: I won't be late. Will you come? Will it be sunny?
content.speakText: I won't be late. Will you come? Will it be sunny?

title: Comparatives and Superlatives

title: Modals: Must, Should, Have To
indexDescription: Give advice, talk about rules, and express obligation.
pageDescription: Use must, should, and have to for advice and rules
goal: Use must, should, and have to for advice, rules, and obligation.

content.title: 1) Should for Advice
content.text: You should sleep more. You shouldn't eat so fast.
content.speakText: You should sleep more. You shouldn't eat so fast.

content.title: 2) Must / Have To
content.text: You must wear a seatbelt. I have to work tomorrow.
content.speakText: You must wear a seatbelt. I have to work tomorrow.

content.title: 3) Don't Have To
content.text: You don't have to come early. We don't have to pay.
content.speakText: You don't have to come early. We don't have to pay.

title: Quantity: Some, Any, Much, Many
indexDescription: Talk about quantity with countable and uncountable nouns.
pageDescription: Talk about quantity in shops, kitchens, and daily life
goal: Use some, any, much, and many with countable and uncountable nouns.

content.title: 1) Countable vs Uncountable
content.text: apples (countable) / water (uncountable); books / money
content.speakText: apples, water, books, money

content.title: 2) Some / Any
content.text: I have some apples. Do you have any milk? I don't have any money.
content.speakText: I have some apples. Do you have any milk? I don't have any money.

content.title: 3) Much / Many
content.text: How many eggs? How much water? There isn't much time.
content.speakText: How many eggs? How much water? There isn't much time.

title: Connectors for Longer Sentences
indexDescription: Link ideas clearly with because, so, but, although, and when.
pageDescription: Connect ideas to speak in longer, clearer sentences
goal: Use connectors to join ideas in longer sentences.

content.title: 1) Common Connectors
content.text: and, but, because, so, although, when, if
content.speakText: and, but, because, so, although, when, if

content.title: 2) Reason and Result
content.text: I stayed home because it rained. It rained, so I stayed home.
content.speakText: I stayed home because it rained. It rained, so I stayed home.

content.title: 3) Contrast
content.text: I was tired, but I finished my work. Although it was cold, we went out.
content.speakText: I was tired, but I finished my work. Although it was cold, we went out.

title: Everyday Conversations and Opinions
indexDescription: Share opinions, agree/disagree, and manage everyday conversations.
pageDescription: Give opinions and manage real-life conversations
goal: Share opinions and keep everyday conversations going.

content.title: 1) Giving Opinions
content.text: I think... In my opinion... I believe... For me...
content.speakText: I think. In my opinion. I believe. For me.

content.title: 2) Agreeing and Disagreeing
content.text: I agree. You're right. I don't think so. I'm not sure.
content.speakText: I agree. You're right. I don't think so. I'm not sure.

content.title: 3) Keeping a Conversation Going
content.text: Really? What about you? That sounds interesting. Tell me more.
content.speakText: Really? What about you? That sounds interesting. Tell me more.
